content.text:
Axios's Node adapter can now send the built-in `FormData` that Node 18+ provides. Before, posting one failed with "Data after transformation must be a string, an ArrayBuffer, a Buffer, or a Stream".

I tested it against a local server on Node 20, using a form with a text field and a `Blob` file. The server received a correct multipart body with the right boundary and a matching `Content-Length`. It also worked with `onUploadProgress` set.

The http adapter and helper tests show 93 passing and 3 failing ("max content length", "upload progress capturing" and "download progress capturing"). Those same three fail when I run the tests on the code without my changes, so I didn't cause them. Running the full unit suite didn't finish within two minutes, so I stopped it; I only ran the http adapter and helper tests.

**What changed:**
- **`lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js` (new):** turns a standard `FormData` into a multipart stream. It escapes field names and normalises line endings to CRLF. It sets `Content-Type` with a generated boundary, or reuses a boundary you already put in `Content-Type`, and sets `Content-Length` when the size is known.
- **`lib/helpers/readBlob.js` (new):** reads the contents of `Blob` and `File` values for that stream.
- **`lib/adapters/http.js`:** standard `FormData` objects now go through that new path. The existing support for the `form-data` npm package is unchanged.
- **`lib/utils.js`:** adds `isSpecCompliantForm` (moved here from `toFormData.js`, which now uses the shared copy) plus a small random-string helper for boundaries.

I didn't update the TypeScript type definitions.
